context:
Goal: run two phone simulators at once safely.
Problem (rule): with PR 3689 (a pull request that lets the smaller phone simulator, the Duo, run beside the larger one, the Pro), a Pro may start beside a Duo when the Mac's five-minute load average is under 100, but a second Duo needs it under 60, and your 12 Nov ruling sims-load-brake-only (the simulator lease is held back by load alone) names only the second-slot bar, so the bar for a mixed pair is your call.
Based on (read): the consultant's reading of PR 3689 as built: a Pro beside a Duo starts under load 100; a second Duo needs load under 60.
Departs from: main — the lease refuses a Duo while the Pro slot is held — a second simulator of any kind starts only when the five-minute load is under 60.
Waiting on: nothing is stopped; PR 3689 merges as built after its lint, and the consultant changes it on your answer.

options.gain: One rule to remember; less risk of overloading the Mac.
options.how: The lease holds every second simulator, mixed pair or two Duos, to a five-minute load under 60.
options.label: The same bar for any second simulator: load under 60 (recommended)
options.lose: A Pro beside a Duo waits more often.

options.label: Keep it as built: under 100 for a Pro beside a Duo, under 60 for a second Duo

ref: consultant message 20:38 CST Nov 18, asking triage to post this question; the reads are the consultant's, not re-read by triage

shown.label: The same bar for any second simulator: load under 60 (recommended)
Keep it as built: under 100 for a Pro beside a Duo, under 60 for a second Duo

title: Should any second phone simulator wait for the same load bar of 60?
why: a gives one rule and less overload risk at the cost of a longer wait for a mixed pair; b starts a mixed pair sooner but keeps two bars. Recommended by the consultant, not owner-typed.
